#!/bin/bash
#
# RelicOS: PortMaster's per-firmware hook. PortMaster.sh and every port
# script source control.txt and then mod_${CFW_NAME}.txt, if it exists
# in the PortMaster folder -- the file PortMaster keeps for KNULLI, muOS
# and ROCKNIX under their names; this one is RelicOS's, and
# /usr/bin/relicos-port copies it here on every launch (a PortMaster
# update that replaces the folder loses it until the next launch).
# Do not edit: the copy in the system image is the one that counts.
#
# The pads. control.txt's get_controls writes the controller table a
# port will use to /tmp/gamecontrollerdb.txt -- for a device it does not
# know by its own heuristics, an EMPTY file (2026.06.23) -- and the port
# then exports that file's content as SDL_GAMECONTROLLERCONFIG, over
# anything the launcher put in the environment; SDL falls back to its
# guess from the evdev codes, which puts "a" on the button printed B.
# RelicOS's launcher maps every pad the ES named, from the ES's own
# es_input.cfg and the pad's BUTTON LAYOUT (relicos-pads --sdl), into
# RELICOS_SDL_PADS: those lines go into that same file here, right after
# get_controls filled it, and the variable the port exports is refreshed.
# PortMaster's interface, gptokeyb (which reads SDL_GAMECONTROLLERCONFIG_FILE)
# and the game then see each pad the way the rest of RelicOS does.
if declare -f get_controls > /dev/null 2>&1; then
  eval "relicos_orig_$(declare -f get_controls)"
  get_controls() {
    relicos_orig_get_controls "$@"
    if [ -n "$RELICOS_SDL_PADS" ] && [ -n "$SDL_GAMECONTROLLERCONFIG_FILE" ]; then
      printf '%s\n' "$RELICOS_SDL_PADS" >> "$SDL_GAMECONTROLLERCONFIG_FILE"
      sdl_controllerconfig="$(< "$SDL_GAMECONTROLLERCONFIG_FILE")"
    fi
  }
fi
